subject: Delta throughput qualification - post-call notes and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-logistics.com>, Priyanka Sharma <pri@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T15:03:00Z
Subject: Delta throughput qualification - post-call notes and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion, lots of useful signals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have a single source of truth.

High-level takeaways (what we heard):
- Primary workload is an interactive tracking assistant used inside the driver app (session lengths ~8–25s).
- Two traffic modes: baseline (steady checks, ~40 qps globally) and crest windows (regional spikes during dispatch surges up to ~750 QPS for 1–3 minute windows).
- Messages are mostly short prompts (~120 tokens input, 40–60 tokens model response) but a small percentage (~6%) are longer multiprompt sessions (400–1,200 tokens).
- Streaming responses are required in the driver UI for perceived latency; tail latency target is 95th ≤ 400ms for first token, end-to-end 95th ≤ 1.2s for full streamed response.

Open questions we agreed to answer:
1) Exact QPS by region during crest windows (sample from last two weeks).
2) Typical concurrency per driver session and the fraction of sessions that upgrade to multiprompt.
3) Any batchable non-streaming flows (e.g., nightly bulk scoring) that could be routed differently.

Immediate next steps (owner):
- Acme: share the anonymized traffic snippet and a small sample of payloads (CSV or gz — required by Monday) — Alex/Priyanka
- Redwood: run quick local profile with similar token mix, produce an initial throughput matrix (tokens/sec, model mix) and propose a pilot footprint (estimated reserved GPUs and expected cost) — Karthik / Jordan — deliver by Wed 13th
- Joint: schedule a 60-min pilot scoping workshop once sample is in (aim Thu or Fri next week) — Jordan to send invite

Attachments: I attached a blank SLO matrix template and a short CSV example we use for profiling.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-logistics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Sharma <pri@acme-logistics.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Delta throughput qualification - post-call notes and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and I attached a 10k-row anonymized snippet as discussed.

Clarifications:
- The 750 QPS crest is for our largest metro cluster (NE region) and lasted ~2m during the last high-demand window (May 2). Other regions show crest windows around 120–220 QPS.
- Concurrency: each driver session opens 1 connection; we have multiplexing in the app so typically a driver will open a second stream if the dispatcher requests additional context (~12% of sessions). Peak concurrent sessions in NE during crest reached ~1800 concurrent streams.
- Token mixes: median input 110 tokens, median output 48 tokens. The multiprompt flows that escalate are ~9% of total and average 680 output tokens.

Included: workload_samples_20260502.csv (anonymized) — let me know if the schema is enough. If you need different windowing or a longer historical slice we can produce it but it will take a day.

Alex
Alex Chen — Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Logistics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-logistics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T14:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Delta throughput qualification - post-call notes and next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the snippet. Quick operational assumptions I'm putting into the profiling run (call these out if any are off):
- Model family: you mentioned preferring an Llama-derivative variant under 8B param; we'll profile a 7B float/8-bit quantized option and a 13B q4_0 variant for comparison.
- Streaming semantics: we'll simulate token-by-token streaming with a 25ms per-token emit target to reflect UI stitching latency; that'll let us estimate first-token vs tail costs.
- Concurrency shaping: we'll run two scenarios — baseline steady 40 QPS across region, and crest ramp to 750 QPS for 2 minutes with a 30s ramp-up/down to mimic real crest hysteresis.
- Caching: assume minimal prefix cache effectiveness for multi-turn sessions (~10% hit) unless you confirm repeated prompts.

Requested from Acme (small ask):
- Can you send a small set (5–10) of the longest multiprompt sessions (de-identified) so we can validate KV-cache behavior and worst-case KV size? Please put in the shared Drive folder linked below.

Deliverables and timeline (tentative):
- Redwood will run synthetic profile runs and return a tokens/sec × model matrix plus an estimated reserved GPU footprint for a 30-day pilot by 2026-05-13.
- Post-profile we’ll propose a pilot MRP (minimum reserved proposal) and a scoped A/B canary plan (how traffic will be split and fallbacks).

Attachments: sample workload_snippets.csv attached (first 50 rows).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-logistics.com>, Priyanka Sharma <pri@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Delta throughput qualification - post-call notes and next steps

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turn. Two quick administrative items before we spin up profiling:
1) Can Acme confirm whether the multiprompt 9% is stable across days or if it's bursty (i.e., sometimes 9%, sometimes 20%) — that affects pilot sizing. If you can flag daily variance for the last 14 days that would be ideal.
2) Priyanka — for procurement, do we need an NDA amendment for the pilot or is the existing MSA sufficient? If not, Jordan/Legal can circulate a one-page amendment.

I'll schedule the scoping workshop for Thursday 2026-05-14 10:00 PT — invite to follow. After profiling results are in (by Wed eve) we'll:
- Share an initial capacity chart (GPU types + expected QPS/tokens/sec)
- Map recommended SLOs (first token 95th, tail, and cost per 1k tokens) and a proposed fallback policy (degrade to smaller model or cached reply for noncritical flows)
- Propose pilot acceptance criteria (latency SLOs + continuity during a synthetic crest)

If everyone is OK with the timeline we'll treat this as the mutual action plan for the pilot (deal: ACME-2026-PILOT-47).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (template)
